1.(a) Correct Option: (i) 1

Explanation: By using the sifting property of the Dirac delta function, we know that:

$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \delta(t - t_0) f(t) dt = f(t_0)$

Here, $t_0 = 0$ and $f(t) = \cos\left(\frac{3t}{2}\right)$. Substituting $t = 0$ into the function gives:

$f(0) = \cos\left(\frac{3(0)}{2}\right) = \cos(0) = 1$

2.(b) Correct Option: (ii) input signal can be uniquely determined by observing the output signal

Explanation:

An invertible system is a system where distinct inputs always produce distinct outputs (a one-to-one mapping). Because every input leads to a unique output, you can work backward—meaning the input signal can be uniquely determined just by observing the output signal.

Solution

Energy signals have finite energy and zero average power, whereas power signals have finite average power and infinite energy.

Here is a direct comparison of the key differences between the two types of signals:

Property / Feature Energy Signal Power Signal
Total Energy ($E$) Finite value ($0 < E < \infty$) Infinite value ($E = \infty$)
Average Power ($P$) Zero ($P = 0$) Finite value ($0 < P < \infty$)
Signal Duration Time-limited (finite duration) Extends to infinity (infinite duration)
Periodicity Generally non-periodic (deterministic) Generally periodic
